h1: Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 — a dark-chic design hotel with a rooftop pool and official day-use, at a price that makes sense
intro: If you want a real hotel with a rooftop pool in the Asok–Sukhumvit corridor without paying four-star rates, Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 is the name that keeps appearing in real guest reviews. It is a 195-room, 3-star design property on Sukhumvit Soi 15 — understated dark-tone rooms with better-than-average cotton-linen bedding, a rooftop pool and Jacuzzi open until 10pm, and a free tuk-tuk shuttle running continuously to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit. Official day-use is bookable via Dayuse.com for around US$46 with rooftop pool access included — a proper hotel check-in, no by-the-hour vibe. Overnight stays start from approx. THB 1,700/night, with a score of 8.7 from 4,380 Booking.com reviews.

body.html: Night Hotel Bangkok has occupied Sukhumvit Soi 15 for several years and attracts a steady stream of repeat guests from across the world. What sets it apart from comparably priced competitors in the neighbourhood is the rooftop outdoor pool with Jacuzzi and sun loungers, open from 8am to 10pm and included in every overnight rate — and, crucially, available for day-use via Dayuse.com at around US$46 with pool access. This is a standard hotel check-in, not a short-time arrangement; the vibe is completely normal.

The soi 15 address is quieter than the main Sukhumvit strip, positioned between BTS Asok and BTS Nana. BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit are roughly 5–7 minutes on foot, but the hotel's free tuk-tuk shuttle removes any walking concern — the little three-wheelers run continuously throughout the day and into the evening, ferrying guests to both stations. Dozens of reviews single this out as genuinely useful, particularly for late-night returns from the Asok–Nana area. Terminal 21 is barely 450 metres away.
"The rooftop pool is lovely — quiet, good views, and the tuk-tuk to BTS Asok made the location feel very easy. Staff were outstanding, the best part of the stay."

Rooms carry a dark, confident design tone — deeper-coloured walls, blackout curtains, 42-inch TVs, mini-bar and desk. The cotton-linen bedding is noticeably softer and heavier than typical 3-star Thai hotels, which most guests appreciate. Room categories run from Bronze King and Gold Twin (the most-booked standard options) through to the Dream Exclusive Suite for couples wanting more space, and a Family Suite Connecting for groups of three or four. One structural point worth knowing upfront: the property spans two buildings across the street from each other. The pool sits in one building; some rooms are in the other. It is a short walk — not inconvenient — but ask at check-in which building you have been assigned if proximity to the pool matters to you.

Breakfast at Flava Restaurant earns consistent praise across review platforms — a generously stocked buffet with both Thai and international options, regularly described as exceeding 3-star expectations. The 24-hour fitness centre is well equipped with treadmills, weights, ellipticals and more. Coran Boutique Spa on-site covers massage and wellness treatments for guests who would rather not go out. Free parking is also available, which is a genuine plus in this part of Sukhumvit.

The dominant theme in guest reviews is the staff. Booking.com's staff category scores 9.4 out of 10 — remarkably high — and multiple detailed reviews describe the team as "exceptional," "proactive," and genuinely invested in helping with everything from room swaps to restaurant recommendations. The two recurring caveats: the mattresses are on the soft side (a handful of guests with back issues wish they were firmer), and a few rooms in the older building show signs of damp during Bangkok's monsoon months. Neither is a deal-breaker for most travellers, but they are worth knowing before you book.

If you are a couple or two friends looking for a design hotel with a rooftop pool and honest 3-star value near Asok, Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 delivers. And if you want to test it before committing to a full night — or just want a private afternoon in the pool without an overnight stay — the Dayuse.com booking route makes that genuinely easy. Book the day-use slot in advance: they are not unlimited.

highlights.title: Rooftop pool + Jacuzzi
highlights.text: Open-air rooftop pool with Jacuzzi and sun loungers, open 8am–10pm. Included with overnight stays. Day-use bookable via Dayuse.com for approx. US$46, pool access included.

highlights.title: Free tuk-tuk to BTS Asok / MRT
highlights.text: The hotel's complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle runs continuously to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit throughout the day. No walking in the heat, no waiting for taxis late at night.

highlights.title: Dark-chic design, quality linen
highlights.text: Confident dark-tone rooms with above-average cotton-linen bedding, 42-inch TV, mini-bar and free Wi-Fi. More considered in its design than most 3-star options at this price point.

honestSummary: Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 is a strong value choice for couples or friends who want a design hotel with a rooftop pool near Asok at a genuine 3-star price — excellent staff, clean rooms with good linen, a breakfast that over-delivers, and a free tuk-tuk shuttle that removes the only real friction of this location. The two-building layout and soft mattresses are the honest caveats; neither is a dealbreaker for most people.
honestChecks: If you need a firm mattress — multiple reviewers flag the beds as too soft for back-pain sufferers. Flag it at check-in and ask whether a firmer option is available; if mattress firmness is a dealbreaker, consider another property.

If you want your room directly adjacent to the pool — the property is split across two buildings. Ask at booking or check-in which building you are in; the walk across the street is not far, but it is worth knowing in advance.

If you want to come for day-use only — book your slot on Dayuse.com in advance, not on arrival. Day-use capacity is limited per day, and walk-ins may be turned away. Day-use does not include breakfast.

tips.title: Use the free tuk-tuk every time
tips.body: The hotel's tuk-tuk shuttle to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit runs throughout the day. Check the schedule with Front Desk on arrival — it saves both the walk and the hassle of finding a taxi late at night.

tips.title: Pool is best on weekday afternoons
tips.body: The rooftop pool is quietest and most photogenic between 2pm and 5pm on weekdays. Weekend mornings and early afternoons get busy. For day-use, book your slot on Dayuse.com — do not leave it to arrival.

tips.title: Ask which building at check-in
tips.body: Tell the front desk you want to be in the building closest to the pool when you check in. Staff will accommodate the request subject to availability — it is worth asking.

tips.title: Include breakfast if the package option is there
tips.body: The breakfast buffet at Flava Restaurant is well regarded and worth having. If a room-with-breakfast package is available, it typically works out cheaper than paying the walk-in rate of approx. THB 530 per person on the day.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15

faq.q: Where is Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 and how close is it to the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 10 Sukhumvit Soi 15, Watthana, Bangkok 10110. BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit are roughly 5–7 minutes on foot, and the hotel runs a complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle to both stations throughout the day. Terminal 21 shopping mall is roughly 450 metres away.

faq.q: Does Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 offer day-use? How do I book it?
faq.a: Yes — official day-use is bookable via Dayuse.com for around US$46, with rooftop pool and Jacuzzi access included. Book in advance as daily slots are limited. Day-use does not include breakfast.

faq.q: What does Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 cost per night?
faq.a: Overnight rates start from approx. THB 1,700/night for a Bronze King Room or Gold Twin Room. Prices vary by season and booking platform — compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before committing. High season (November–February) typically runs 20–30% higher.

faq.q: What is the rooftop pool like at Night Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: It is an outdoor pool on the roof, open from 8am to 10pm, with a Jacuzzi and sun loungers alongside. Views over the Sukhumvit neighbourhood are good. The pool is included free for overnight guests; day-use guests book via Dayuse.com for approx. US$46.

faq.q: Who is Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 best for?
faq.a: It is a strong match for couples or two friends wanting a design hotel with a pool near Asok–Sukhumvit at a genuine 3-star price. Day-use is ideal for anyone wanting a private afternoon by the pool without an overnight stay. It is less ideal for guests who need a firm mattress or want their room directly attached to the pool area without crossing between buildings.
